chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: @Sanketh Menda thanks! Revocation is where I'd most like eyes. It's group-local: one of the user's remaining devices commits a newer log, the group's record of each user's head only moves forward, and the Commit that raises it has to remove the leaves the new head drops. The weak spots are a group with none of the user's devices in it, which never hears of the revocation (the stale-log section), and ReInit or branching, which don't carry the record (Section 7). Happy to compare notes with the MTC revocation work.

chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-00 (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential/): today the provider's Authentication Service decides which devices are a user's, so in federated groups (MIMI) any member's provider can add a device under that user's name. This defines a credential where the user authorizes each device: it carries the user's did:webvh log, a hash-chained signed history of device keys any member can check offline, plus group rules so every member reaches the same validity decision and revocation propagates through ordinary Commits. Open issues are in Section 7. Reading notes: https://github.com/MarkAtwood/mls-didwebvh-credential/tree/main/ietf127. Comments welcome on mls@; is there interest in working on this?

chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: @Rohan Mahy Small in practice: about 1.5 KB per log entry, one entry per device change, so a user with ten device changes is ~15 KB. The 1 MiB is a hard cap so every member rejects the same oversized log, not an expected size. The real cost is that each leaf carries its user's whole log, repeated across that user's devices; credential by reference, as you raised for SlimMLS, would fix that, and there's no log compaction yet. Happy to lower the cap.

chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: @Orie Steele The DID method isn't the core. What matters is a key the user holds authorizing each device, with a hash-chained history members can check offline. did:webvh already has that, which is why -00 uses it, but I'd happily do it as CWT/COSE with SCITT-style signed statements instead; that's question 1 on the slides.

chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: +1 on opportunistic channels. Receipts and similar metadata are mostly unencrypted today, so a cheap channel with weaker guarantees is a real improvement, as long as the draft is clear it's two clients and not two users.
